title: Projection compatibility of the middle graph constituent
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, f:X→Y a morphism of arbitrary schemes, c a supplied open/proper compactification and t=(a,e,p) a proper/open/proper presentation of f. Form the concrete graph presentations t1,t2 and comparison factors B1,B2,D of [def-sf-graph-projection-stages]. For every M in D(X_et,A) and K in D(Y_et,A), tensor D_M with K and then apply the successive word projection of the second graph presentation t2. The result equals the first graph-word projection for t1 followed by D evaluated at M tensor Lf*K. These are the exact sfGraphWordProjection coefficient compositors [def-sf-etale-graph-word-projection]. No other graph constituent is used in this assertion, and no qc, Noetherianity or boundedness is required.

proof.text: Take the common intersection of the supporting opens and its two projections u1 and u2. Each proper graph si factors as s12 ui. Apply the identity-top proper/open factor projection square to each factorization. The pullback-composition associativity identity transports their coefficient maps to the single coefficient map for s12 followed by the common open.

Apply open projection composition to ui followed by bi. Transport along pullback.condition, identifying the common open u1 b1=u2 b2. Paste the inverse first factor square, the first associator, the open-composition square, the inverse second associator, and the second factor square. Compatibility is preserved under inverse, composition, associator, and whiskering, by naturality and cancellation of isomorphisms. This is exactly locallyClosedGraphMiddle with its specified factors.

Whisker by the common outer proper direct image. Naturality of its projection pastes the resulting square with the inner one. Expanding the canonical coefficient compositors identifies the composite strengths with sfGraphWordProjection for the two supplied graph presentations. The outer associators are identity components, and their cancellation gives precisely sfGraphMiddleIso_projection. No proper projection map is inverted.
